title: A provincial view of the record audience
summary: Matassa admits he did not appreciate who would buy the records, thinking of sales from New Orleans to Pensacola until out-of-town producers demanded more.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: I mean, you didn't, you didn't realize, did you realize that, wait, this is going to be a record and people are going to listen to this and people are going to buy it? I did that.

You're going to buy it. But we, you know, we were generally thinking until, until the, the, the, the, the guys started coming in and demanding stuff that, that they could sell in, in Iowa and, you know, it was more of, of, we're going to sell this from, from, from here to, to Patsicola.
Yeah, I had a very provincial attitude, I think, in that sense. Yeah.
Well, but it's understandable. I think a lot, I think a lot of people.
I think some of the record companies did.
